issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Module-level type F: the process dies with an uncaught Go panic `panic: runtime error: index out of range [-1]` (projects/package_compilation.go:174 re-panics the desugar panic), with a goroutine trace and no diagnostic. The local-variable variant gives `fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: panic during desugaring`. The clean-context spec check says the program is valid (§5.6.2 allows omitting param names in a function-type-descriptor; §6.15 takes the default from the declared type) and should print 2 then 4. The crash happens in the front end (desugaring) before BIR, so frontend + frontend-crash. Related but not duplicates: #1227, #1232.

issues.title: [Bug]: lexer treats non-ASCII characters as hex digits (INTERNAL_ERROR on `0x1Ł`, invalid `\u{Ł}` escape accepted)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: `0x1Ł` gives `fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: failed to parse numeric literal` (a diagnostic, not a Go panic, so no frontend-crash). `"\u{Ł}"` compiles and prints `\u{Ł}`, and `int \u{Ł}` compiles and prints 1. The clean-context spec check says all three must be compile errors (HexDigit is ASCII only; NumericEscape needs HexDigit+). Cause confirmed in the code: `isHexDigit(byte(reader.Peek()))` in parser/lexer.go (also xml_lexer.go and documentation_lexer.go). Lexer bug → frontend. Related: #1054 (same INTERNAL_ERROR text, different cause), #1348 (closed).

issues.title: [Bug]: `toString()`/`toBalString()` method call on an object-typed receiver gives "method not found"
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: method not found: toString
  --> 1621.bal:10:16
   |
10 |     io:println(q.toString() == value:toString(q));
   |                ^^^^^^^^^^^^

error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: method not found: toBalString
  --> 1621.bal:11:16
   |
11 |     io:println(q.toBalString() == value:toBalString(q));
   |                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: `SEMANTIC_ERROR: method not found: toString` / `toBalString`. The clean-context spec check says the program is valid (§6.16 falls back to lang.value when the object type has no member of that name and lang.object has no such function) and prints true twice. The failure is in method-call resolution in the type checker, not in the lang.value implementation → frontend rather than langlib. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: default expressions in function type descriptors are not type-checked or isolation-checked
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: `function (int a = "s")` compiles and prints `s` (a string bound to an int parameter); `isolated function (int a = gv)` with a mutable module var compiles and prints 5. The clean-context spec check says both must be compile errors: the default must belong to the parameter type, and §5.6.2 requires an isolated function type's defaults to meet isolated-function rules (§7.3.5). Missing semantic checks → frontend. Sibling of #1119 (the same gap for method declarations in object types) and related to #1117, #1227; not a duplicate.

issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: `initializer of an isolated variable must be an isolated expression` for `pair(1)` and `factory.make(2)`. The clean-context spec check says the program is valid (§6.15 and §6.16 isolated function/method-call rules) and prints [1,2] then [2]. Semantic analysis rejects a valid program → frontend. Siblings, not duplicates: #1591 (`new C(args)`), #1429 (langlib call), #1501 (conditional expr).

issues.title: [Bug]: template expressions with isolated interpolations are not isolated expressions
issues.output: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: initializer of an isolated variable must be an isolated expression --> 1628.bal:5:24 | 5 | isolated xml element = xml `${n}`; | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: `initializer of an isolated variable must be an isolated expression` for xml `${n}` with `final int n`. The clean-context spec check says the program is valid (§6.2.6 template-expr is isolated if all its subexpressions are isolated) and prints 1. Semantic analysis rejects a valid program → frontend. Sibling of #1501, #1591, #1627; not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: isolated class field initializer can alias a mutable module-level value
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: it compiles and prints 99, so the isolated object's private state is mutated outside a lock. The clean-context spec check says it must be a compile error: §8.6 applies the explicitly-isolated object-constructor rules, and §6.8.1 says every field-initializer must be an isolated expression; `g: int[]` is not one. Missing semantic check → frontend. Sibling of #940 (the same rule for field assignments in init), not a duplicate.

notes: Skipped issues were in earlier reports and have not been updated since. All 8 new issues reproduce on main and are valid by the spec; every one is a frontend issue, and #1618 also crashes the front end with a Go panic. Validity was decided by a clean-context subagent that saw only the reproducers. No duplicates found.
